exposure: Nursing student mothers' perception of desired delivery type
Academic knowledge about benefits of vaginal birth
Financial situation of the parturient woman
Control of choice by health professional
outcome: Discrepancy between desired and actual delivery route
Predominance of cesarean section as performed procedure
cohort: The study included 16 nursing student mothers who had experienced the parturition process.
finding: An unsatisfactory discrepancy was identified between the mother's preference for vaginal delivery (due to academic knowledge) and the actual delivery, with cesarean section being predominant due to complications, fears, financial situation, and control by health professionals.
mod_finding: An unsatisfactory discrepancy was found between the desired vaginal delivery route and the actual predominantly performed cesarean section, influenced by complications, fears, financial situation, and lack of autonomy.
